Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Neither AWS, Azure nor Google Cloud has a region in West Africa; the nearest hyperscale regions to Niger are in South Africa (Cape Town/Johannesburg), roughly 4,000km away. Even Microsoft ruled out (Dec 2025) building a Nigeria data centre, confirming continued reliance on distant South African regions across the wider West Africa sub-region. Original had no source cited, but the score of 2 (served remotely, >100ms latency) is well supported and confirmed unchanged.

Definition: The country's overall cybersecurity preparedness, based on the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index (GCI). Covers legal measures, technical measures, organisational measures, capacity development, and cooperation. Essential for trust in stored data and digital services.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: ITU's Global Cybersecurity Index 2024 gives Niger a score of 41.86 (per statbase.org, citing ITU as source; corroborated by the official ITU-sourced tier table on indicators.govmu.org). This falls in the metadata's 40-59 'Establishing' band, not the 20-39 'Evolving' band originally coded, so recalculated to 3. Note for human review: ITU's own real-world GCI tier chart actually places Niger in Tier 4 'Evolving' because ITU's real cut-off for 'Establishing' is a score of >=55, not >=40 as implied by this metadata's Format column — there is a mismatch between the metadata's numeric bands and ITU's own tier labels that the lead may want to reconcile.

Definition: The maturity of the country's technology startup ecosystem, based on the number of tech startups, venture capital activity, accelerators/incubators, and the presence of a supportive ecosystem. Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.
Value Name: Nascent (very few tech startups, no visible VC activity)
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: CIPMEN (est. 2014, Niger's leading incubator) has incubated 222 companies and trained nearly 8,000 people, with several small tech ventures in its portfolio (Niger Digital, Global IT, Sadit Technologies), which is more than 'very few' startups. However, Niger is entirely absent from the Partech Africa, AVCA and Africa: The Big Deal funding trackers for 2023-2025, confirming no visible disclosed VC activity. Recalculated to 2 (Emerging: some startups, limited funding, 1-2 hubs).

revision_notes: At least five active hubs identified: CIPMEN, Cabinet Hub Zinder and STRAT-CORE Plus (all listed as AfriLabs members), plus Sahel Incubateur, MouganiLab, and the government/AFD/EU-funded Cité de l'Innovation de Sadoré (opened 2022, includes a Fab Lab and Niger's first coding school, Codeloccol). Definition: The size and vibrancy of the local software developer and technology professional community. Measured through proxies such as GitHub activity, Stack Overflow representation, local tech meetup groups, and developer surveys. Indicates the country's capacity to build and maintain digital systems locally.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: GDG Niamey (597 members) runs regular events (DevFest Niamey, 'Build with AI'), and a GDG Cloud Niamey chapter has since formed; CIPMEN also runs the Codeloccol coding school. Individual developer GitHub/LinkedIn profiles confirm an active, if small, community. This is a small but growing community rather than 'negligible'; recalculated to 2 (Emerging, <1,000 active developers).

revision_notes: At least five institutions offer ICT/CS/telecoms programmes: Université Abdou Moumouni (Licence Informatique), Université Islamique du Niger (Faculté des Sciences et Techniques, 1,200+ ICT/telecoms graduates since 2009), École Supérieure des Télécommunications (EST-Niger), Université de Dosso's IUT (Informatique & Télécoms department, opened 2016), and private EPI Niger (Informatique de Gestion, Génie Logiciel and Cybersécurité programmes).
